decisions.statement: The change assigns problems in metadata-defined members to their defining project and centrally suppresses the corresponding consuming-compilation diagnostics, including all diagnostics without an in-compilation primary location.
decisions.whyHuman: A test can observe where a diagnostic appears, but it cannot determine the desired diagnostic ownership, acceptable analyzer noise, or compatibility policy for location-less diagnostics. The reported valid repro does not specify what should happen to invalid members in a referenced assembly.
options: Drop diagnostics whose primary location is absent or outside the current compilation and rely on the defining project, as implemented and documented.
Report a consuming-project diagnostic at the source member that references the metadata type when such a location exists.
Preserve location-less or external-location diagnostics and handle analyzer host restrictions separately.
Restrict suppression to the known metadata-member diagnostic sites instead of applying it to every diagnostic passed through TypeCollector.reportDiagnostic.

decisions.statement: Regression verification uses in-memory compilations and metadata images, adds an explicit attributed resolver to each usage source, and checks generator hint names instead of running the original two-project command-line build.
decisions.whyHuman: A test cannot settle which verification fidelity is proportionate for this defect or whether an in-memory Roslyn harness is an acceptable substitute for project-reference and command-line build integration; that is a test-design tradeoff.
options: Use the in-memory metadata-reference harness with explicit resolver declarations, as implemented.
Reproduce the two project files with dotnet build and inspect the consuming assembly for its resolver.
Keep the focused in-memory tests and add a separate two-project build integration test.
Use an in-memory harness but also cover the scenario without an explicit GeneratedMessagePackResolver declaration.

findings.statement: BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull can be silently dropped for a current-compilation property whose declaration syntax is ParameterSyntax, such as a positional record property. The nearby member-key path explicitly handles ParameterSyntax, but GetPropertyIdentifierLocation recognizes only PropertyDeclarationSyntax; it therefore returns null for that case, and the new central wrapper does not forward a diagnostic with Location.None.

citations.quote: var identifier = (syntax as PropertyDeclarationSyntax)?.Identifier ?? (syntax as ParameterSyntax)?.Identifier;

findings.statement: None of the three new metadata regression scenarios covers generation without an explicit resolver declaration. Every usage source adds [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] to a custom partial resolver, and the common assertion looks for that resolver's hint name, leaving the issue's no-explicit-resolver shape unrepresented in the added tests.

The added helper does not exercise a two-project dotnet build or inspect a built consuming assembly. It emits the defining source to an in-memory image, invokes CSharpGeneratorDriver on another in-memory compilation, and checks generated hint names, so command-line project-reference integration and physical app.dll contents remain outside this regression coverage.
